ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
3.4.4 Participating Financial Institutions

Scheduled Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Small
Finance Banks, Cooperative Banks, Non-Banking Finance
Companies and Micro Finance Institutions, are eligible to
lend under this Scheme. The Lending Institutions will be
encouraged to use their network of field functionaries i.e.,
Business Correspondents/ Associates to ensure maximum
coverage of the Scheme.

3.5 Incentives for Digital Transaction

(i) The Scheme aims to digitally empower the
beneficiaries by facilitating them to adopt digital
transactions. An amount of Re. 1 per eligible digital
transaction (upto a maximum of 100 eligible
transaction) monthly will be credited to the
beneficiary’s bank account in DBT mode through
Aadhaar Payment Bridge System (APBS). Here,
eligible transaction means a digital pay-out or receipt
in the bank account of the beneficiary.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(ii) The Scheme envisages to incentivize digital
transactions undertaken by the artisans and
craftspeople through cashbacks. The online
transaction trail so created is expected to enhance the
credit score of skilled workers for supporting their
future credit needs. This incentive is an attempt to
promote a new digital culture among the
Vishwakarmas with regard to embracing digital
payments ecosystem.

3.6 Marketing Support

Creating market linkages for the Vishwakarmas is a
critical step in improving their livelihood and quality of
life. The National Committee for Marketing (NCM) shall
provide marketing and branding support for the products
of the artisans and craftspeople registered under the
Scheme. Marketing Support in the form of quality
certification, branding, advertising, publicity and other
marketing activities would be extended to the
beneficiaries to improve their linkage to value chain of

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
MSMEs and established companies. The composition
of NCM, will include marketing experts and is given in
Annexure-B. The NCM may engage services of
professional agencies/entities for market support
activities for the beneficiaries.

The NCM will have a dedicated corpus of funds for
carrying out marketing support activities and it will
assist the Vishwakarmas in the following:

a. Quality Certification: The NCM shall ensure that the
quality of products being marketed and distributed
through its channels is as per the market standards.
This will also motivate the Vishwakarmas to improve
the quality of their products and services to make them
marketable and competitive in domestic as well as
international markets. Endeavours will be made for
creating a certification system for quality to improve
their linkage to domestic and global value chains. The
beneficiaries shall be eligible for assistance for Quality
Certification which will enhance the quality of their
products and services and set standards for
competence.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
b. Branding & Promotion: The NCM will support in
creating a physical and online presence of products
and services of the Vishwakarmas. The products are
envisaged to be sold under a common brand identity to
enhance credibility and market acceptability. It will
promote the brand through digital advertising and
social media campaigns. It will also support in
managing the distribution channels with added
operations and logistics support.

c. E-commerce: The NCM will enable cataloguing and
on boarding of the products and services of the
Vishwakarmas on popular e-commerce platforms like
Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC)
platform and make efforts for e-commerce linkage with
GeM, Khadi India, MSME Mart, etc. The beneficiaries
will be eligible for receiving assistance regarding
on-boarding related expenses on e-commerce
platforms.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
d. Market Linkages: The NCM will encourage
collaboration with buyers through integration of
Vishwakarmas into the supply chains, creation of
backward and forward linkages, packaging and
logistics support, etc. Efforts will be made to promote
the use of digital marketing for wider reach and
publicity of the Scheme to reach beneficiaries in
remote areas.

e. Exporters & Traders: The NCM will facilitate linking
the beneficiaries with the suitable exporters and
traders operating under this sector. This will be
achieved through collaborations with Industry Bodies
and Export Promotion Councils.

f. Trade Fairs: The Scheme will facilitate participation
of beneficiaries in trade fairs, exhibitions, etc. by
bringing the beneficiaries under the ambit of market
access schemes of other ministries. Through
inter-ministerial convergence, the Vishwakarmas shall
be provided access to opportunities for participation in
trade fairs. Vishwakarmas who would like to
participate in domestic and international exhibitions
will be required to register on the Udyam Registration
Portal to avail these benefits under Procurement and
Marketing Support Scheme (PMSS) or International
Cooperation scheme of MoMSME.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
g. Assistance for collective display of PM
Vishwakarma Products: NCM may consider
providing assistance for collective display of PM
Vishwakarma Products to associations/ trusts
/societies of the artisan groups registered under any
State or Central Governments Act in the selected
trades.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
4. Eligibility

(i) An artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools
and engaged in one of the family-based traditional trades
specified in Para 2.3, in the unorganized sector on
self-employment basis, shall be eligible for registration
under PM Vishwakarma.

(ii) The minimum age of the beneficiary should be 18 years
on the date of registration.

(iii) The beneficiary should be engaged in the trades
concerned on the date of registration and should not have
availed loans under similar credit-based schemes of
Central Government or State Government for
self-employment/ business development, e.g. PMEGP,
PM SVANidhi, Mudra, in the past 5 years. However, the
beneficiaries of MUDRA and SVANidhi who have repaid
their loan, will be eligible under PM Vishwakarma. This
period of 5 years will be calculated from the date of
sanction of the loan.

(iv) The registration and benefits under the Scheme shall be
restricted to one member of the family. For availing
benefits under the Scheme, a ‘family’ is defined as
consisting of the husband, wife and unmarried children.
(v) A person in government service and their family members
shall not be eligible under the Scheme.

text:
5. Registration Process

5.1 Application for enrolment

5.1.1 MoMSME in association with CSCs (Common
Service Centres) shall enrol the beneficiary families.
Further, an Aadhaar authenticated and centralized PM
Vishwakarma portal shall act as the facilitator for this
exercise along with a PM Vishwakarma mobile app for
enabling smooth operations of the Scheme.

5.1.2 The Ministry of Labour & Employment
(MoLE) maintains the National Database of
Unorganized Workers (NDUW) on the e-Shram
portal, which is mapped with National Classification of
Occupations (NCO). This e-Shram mapped database
will be primarily used for identification of potential
beneficiaries falling in the trade categories covered
under PM Vishwakarma. These artisans and
craftspeople families will be identified and encouraged
to register under the Scheme.

5.1.3 Besides the above, any eligible person, not
covered under e-Shram database shall also be eligible
to enrol in the Scheme by making an online application
through CSCs or online self-application on the PM
Vishwakarma Portal.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
5.1.4 The enrolment of beneficiaries shall be done by
seeking applications through CSCs under MeitY at the
Gram Panchayat and Urban Local Bodies level as well as
by an online application through the portal. This
exercise will also help in capturing the details of
eligible families of artisans and craftspeople besides
collecting relevant details such as bank account and
purpose and amount of loan, etc. The eligible
beneficiaries are required to get themselves enrolled
through nearest CSC in their area. The following is the
list of documents or information to be provided by the
beneficiaries:

(i) Required documents or information: The
beneficiaries need to produce documents like
Aadhaar, mobile number, bank details, ration card
for the registration.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
a. In case of a beneficiary not having a ration card,
they would be required to produce Aadhaar
cards of all family members. (Para 4 (iv) of the
guidelines on Eligibility may be referred to for
definition of family).
b. If beneficiary does not have bank account, they
will be first required to open a bank account for
which handholding shall be done by the CSC.

(ii) Additional documents or information: The
beneficiaries may be required to provide
additional documents or information as per the
requirements prescribed by the MoMSME.

5.1.5 There shall be no fees or charges for enrolment
under PM Vishwakarma. The entire cost of enrolments
through the CSC under the Scheme and subsequent
registration and issue of certificate/ID card shall be borne
by the Government.

5.1.6 Steps for Registration Process will be as follows:

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(i) The registration shall be done by seeking
applications through Common Service Centres
(CSCs) as well as open online application through
Aadhaar based biometric authenticated PM
Vishwakarma portal. The portal will have
convergence with various Government portals
including Skill India Digital through API. A
multi-lingual helpline will be available on the
portal to ensure that the information is
disseminated to everyone across the country
without any language barrier.

(ii) The beneficiary can apply either on their own or
with the help of the CSCs through Village Level
Entrepreneurs (VLEs) or Enumerators.

(iii) Further, the CSCs will also provide handholding
support to the beneficiaries to assess their key
requirements and choose from the varied benefits
available under the Scheme. At the time of
application, the beneficiaries will be made aware
of the Skill Upgradation component of the
Scheme.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(iv) The beneficiary shall furnish their Aadhaar-seeded
bank account details at the time of application. This
shall be considered as their preferred bank account
for availing any monetary benefit under any
component of PM Vishwakarma.

(v) At every stage of intervention under this Scheme,
Aadhaar authentication would be mandatory.
Aadhaar authentication will be done through
biometric by CSCs.

(vi) The portal will also provide link for registration
under Udyam Assist Portal which is the registration
portal for Informal Micro Enterprises which do not
have PAN. The applicants who have PAN and those
who wish to be registered on the Udyam
Registration Portal for MSMEs will also have an
option for the same.

(vii) The beneficiaries would be encouraged to onboard
on GeM Portal. Further, the Scheme would also be
advertised on GeM Portal. This will provide
encouragement and support to the Vishwakarmas
in getting access to market. Through GeM the
products will be made available freely for
procurement.

(viii) Submission of application by the beneficiary shall be
followed by a three-step verification which, if
successful, will lead to registration under PM
Vishwakarma.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
5.1.7 All registrations under PM Vishwakarma will be
Aadhaar-based and the authentication will be through
biometric. Notification to beneficiaries on disbursement of
incentives will be done through SMS.

5.2 Verification

There will be a three-tier verification and approval process
for the registration of beneficiaries:

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
5.2.1 Stage 1: Verification at Gram Panchayat or
ULB level
The first step of screening for the artisans and
craftspeople registered under PM Vishwakarma will
be through the head of Gram Panchayat/ Chairman of
Village Council or Executive Head/ Administrator of
the Urban Local Body. The Head of Panchayat can use
services of Gram Sevak/Panchayat Secretary in
screening and verifying the details provided by the
beneficiaries. The Head of Gram Panchayat will also
ascertain that the beneficiary has been traditionally
engaged in the trade on self-employment basis. The
verification shall include screening of family details
mentioned by the beneficiary to ensure that only one
eligible person is covered from a family. The same
shall be applicable for the Executive Head in ULB.
The details collected by VLEs will be certified by the
Head of Gram Panchayat in the villages or the
Executive Head of ULBs.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
5.2.2 Stage 2: Vetting and Recommendation by the
District Implementation Committee
The registration verified by the Head of Gram
Panchayat or the Executive Head will be forwarded
online to the District Implementation Committee.
The second step of verification will be done by the
District Implementation Committee which will ensure
proper vetting and recommendation of the
applications made by the beneficiaries.

5.2.3 Stage 3: Approval by the Screening Committee
The final approval for registration of beneficiaries
shall be accorded by the Screening Committee after
due diligence and consideration of the
recommendation made by the District
Implementation Committee. The Screening
Committee will be chaired by an officer of the field
formation of the Office of DC-MSME and will have
members including State Lead Bank Manager,
representatives of MSDE, State Departments of
MSME/Industry and Panchayat Raj as members in
each State/UT to oversee the registration process.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
Following are the terms of reference of the
Screening Committee:
(a) To accord final approval of the beneficiaries for
registration under PM Vishwakarma after
satisfying itself as to their eligibility.

(b) To ensure that the enrolment and verification
process is conducted without undue delays.

(c) To ensure that only eligible beneficiaries in the
trades covered under PM Vishwakarma are
onboarded.

(d) To take or suggest appropriate remedial
measures, if required, for better or more
efficient implementation of the Scheme.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
6.1 PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID
Card

After a successful three-step verification, the artisans and
craftspeople will formally registered under this Scheme as
Vishwakarmas. They will receive a Digital ID, a PM
Vishwakarma Digital Certificate and a PM Vishwakarma
ID Card. The certificate will enable the applicants’
recognition as a Vishwakarma, making them eligible to
avail all the benefits under the Scheme.

6.2 Skill Upgradation

(i) Database of the registered beneficiaries under PM
Vishwakarma shall be shared on a real time basis
through the PM Vishwakarma Portal with MSDE
which shall be responsible for skill verification,
training and certification of beneficiaries. MSDE
shall ensure provisioning of field level institutional
arrangement for upskilling the beneficiaries within
the MSDE ecosystem and/or accredited/ affiliated
skill training institutions.

(ii) The training shall be imparted at vocational training
centres, established/affiliated to MSDE, training
centres of MoRD/NIRD, etc.

(iii) MSDE would ensure the quality of trainers
providing training to beneficiaries under the
Scheme.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(iv) MSDE will design and administer tailor-made
Training programmes relevant to skill upgradation
and modernization needs of the Vishwakarmas
already possessing traditional skill sets and
competencies. Further, proficient senior artisans
and master craftspeople having high skill level will
be involved by MSDE as master trainers. This will
strengthen the Guru - Shishya parampara and will
encourage and enhance skill dissemination from
master craftsmen to multiple beneficiaries in the
trades, in a quality assured manner.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(v) MSDE will facilitate the organization of training at
the nearest possible place from the beneficiaries’
location so that organizing training is feasible and
convenient for both beneficiaries’ and Training
Institutions. This will be ordinarily carried out at a
district level. However, for certain low population
trades, centres may be set up in neighbouring
districts or industrial clusters. Mobilization for Basic
and Advanced Training will be done by States/DIC.

(vi) After, skill verification at training centres, the
beneficiary will become eligible for toolkit incentive
which will be immediately followed by basic training
at the same centres. Further, the beneficiary will
also become eligible for training stipend, which will
be paid after the completion of 5-7 days basic skill
training. A beneficiary shall be eligible for availing
Advanced Skill Training only after successful
completion of Basic Skill Training. The training
stipend shall be credited by MSDE into the Aadhaar
linked bank account of the beneficiary through DBT
mode.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(vii) A Skill Upgradation Committee led by MSDE, with
members from MoMSME along with experts and
lead practitioners drawn from different trades will
monitor the quality of skill training.

6.3 Toolkit Incentive

The beneficiaries who have successfully undergone skill
verification under the ‘Skill Upgradation’ component of
the Scheme, will be eligible for toolkit incentive of Rs.
15,000 through e-RUPI/e-vouchers for purchase, from
designated centres, of improved tools suitable for the
occupation practiced by the Vishwakarma.

6.4 Credit Support
6.4.1 Enterprise Development Loan

(i) The preferred Bank/ Financial Institution of the
beneficiary will sanction and disburse the
‘Enterprise Development Loans’ to the beneficiaries

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
on the PM Vishwakarma portal upon receiving
applications.

(ii) No collateral shall be required to avail the loan
from a Lending Institution/ Bank under the PM
Vishwakarma Scheme.

(iii) PAN requirements for the credit facilities shall be
as per the banking norms.

(iv) Credit information report will be required for
those who have a credit history, for availing
benefits under the credit component, so as to
exclude any defaulter from again availing credit
under the Scheme.

(v) In case of a beneficiary not having a credit
history, the Banks or Financial Institutions shall
not exclude them from availing credit and they
shall also not insist upon Credit Information
Report.

(vi) No prepayment penalty shall be charged from
artisans and craftspeople after 6 months of loan
disbursement.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(vii) The disbursal of credit under the Scheme will be
linked with attainment of specific milestones of
training. The beneficiaries will be eligible for
first Loan Tranche on completion of 5 days Basic
Skill Training provided by MSDE under PM
Vishwakarma. The second Loan Tranche will be
available to skilled beneficiaries who maintain a
standard loan account and have adopted digital
transactions in their business or have taken
Advanced Skill Training.

(viii) The beneficiary will be eligible for second
tranche loan when first tranche loan is fully
repaid. Further, the second loan shall not be
granted before six months of the disbursement of
first tranche loan.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
6.4.2 Concessional Interest and Subvention

(i) The beneficiaries will be charged effective interest at a
fixed rate of 5%. The benefit of entire interest
subvention of upto 8% shall be passed on upfront to
the beneficiaries by MoMSME through banks.

(ii) The Credit Oversight Committee under the
chairmanship of Secretary, DFS may revise the
subvention cap of 8% keeping in view the prevailing
interest rates.

(iii) Advance release of interest subvention to the banks
will be done by MoMSME through an escrow account
or placement of advance funds with the participating
banks or any other suitable mechanism in consultation
with the DFS. For effective monitoring of interest
subvention and ensuring that reimbursement is paid
only for Standard Accounts, the bank will maintain
interest data in Customer Induced Format rather than
System Induced Format.

(iv) The lenders will be required to submit monthly
returns for interest subvention for each financial year.
Subvention will only be provided in respect of those
accounts of borrowers, which are Standard (non-NPA
as per extant RBI guidelines) on respective claim
dates and only for those months during which the
account has remained Standard.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(v) Banks are required to submit quarterly audited
reconciliation certificate to the SIDBI/ Agency
maintaining escrow account for interest subvention
claims.

6.4.3 Credit Guarantee

(i) At the time of sanction and disbursal of loans, the
banks will upload the data on the PM Vishwakarma
portal. From the portal, CGTMSE shall be able to
capture the data through API and issue the
guarantees. The claims against the guarantee shall be
lodged by the banks on CGTMSE portal. Once the
payment is made by CGTMSE, the details will be
updated on the PM Vishwakarma portal. CGTMSE

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
shall be required to share a status report with the
MoMSME on a monthly basis.

(ii) The periodicity of filing of claims by Lending
Institutions shall be quarterly. All the
participating Lending Institutions shall be
eligible to avail this guarantee cover without any
charges.

(iii) CGTMSE shall be reimbursed for the cost of
Annual Guarantee Fee for the loans sanctioned to
beneficiaries under PM Vishwakarma.

6.5 Incentive for Digital transactions

(i) The beneficiaries shall be provided incentives for
promoting digital transactions through UPI. The
business UPI IDs of the Vishwakarmas shall be captured
in the portal at the time of registration.
(ii) For those beneficiaries not having access to QR code and
no UPI ID, they will be provided QR Codes and UPI ID
free of cost through Digital Payment Aggregators (DPA)
e.g. Paytm, Bharat Pe, Phone Pe, etc. The DPAs shall be
suitably incentivized through PIDF Scheme of RBI or
through MoMSME as per incentives being provided
under PM SVANidhi or as decided by MoMSME

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(iii) Efforts to integrate with different platforms of recognized
Digital Payments Platforms, including NPCI (for BHIM),
Unified Payments Interface (UPI), RuPay Debit Cards,
developed by National Payments Corporation of India
(NPCI), BHIM Aadhaar Pay, Bharat Bill Payment System,
etc. shall be made.

(iv) The UPI IDs shall be shared with NPCI and digital
transaction partners for data on the number of
transactions for calculation of incentive amount. SIDBI
will generate the payment file as per data received from
NPCI and send it further for payment to beneficiary.
MoMSME shall make the payment.

(v) The mobile number and UPI ID both shall be taken as
identifier for data on the number of transactions for
calculation of incentive amount. The bank account
through which digital transactions are made may also be
taken for calculation of incentive in this regard.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(vi) The incentive amount shall be transferred to the
beneficiaries’ Aadhaar linked bank account through DBT.

6.6 Marketing Support

(i) The NCM shall facilitate Marketing Support to the
beneficiaries based on the support area selected by
the beneficiary on the PM Vishwakarma portal in
the following aspects:
a. Create physical and online presence for the
products and services of the Vishwakarmas

b. List products on e-commerce portals
c. Brand building
d. Connect Vishwakarmas to exporters and
traders
e. Ensure participation of Vishwakarmas in trade
fairs and exhibition
f. Provide support for ensuring quality of
products
g. Packaging support and other common use
facilities
h. Design and development support
i. Providing support for identifying Government
infrastructure which can be used as retail
space for display of products

(ii) NCM shall reimburse the cost to the beneficiaries in
the following areas:
a. Onboarding on e-commerce platforms
b. Quality certifications
c. Participation in trade fair

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(iii) The NCM shall also support in the formation of
Artisan Producer Organizations (APOs) and help
them in availing retail infrastructure in
Government buildings or in reimbursement of
rental costs incurred by APOs on select basis.
(iv) In this backdrop, a Committee for Standardization
and Quality Control shall also be constituted for
ensuring standardization and quality control of the
products and services.

text:
8. Implementation Framework

A three-tier Implementation Framework at the National, State
and District levels, i.e. the National Steering Committee, State
Monitoring Committee and District Implementation
Committee, respectively has been set up for implementation of
PM Vishwakarma. The operational guidelines of the Scheme,
containing the process flow from registration to disbursal of
benefits along with the templates, will be formulated by the
National Steering Committee and approved by MoMSME. An
online monitoring system or dashboard shall be put in place for
real time monitoring

8.1 National Steering Committee (NSC)

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
The National Steering Committee (NSC) shall be the Apex
Committee constituted by the MoMSME. The NSC will be
empowered to take all major policy and strategy decisions
with respect to the implementation of the Scheme and
approve any modifications required in the Scheme, like
inclusion of further categories of trades. The committee
meeting will be convened at least twice a year for a
Scheme-level review, course corrections or to discuss any
other agenda as deemed important in the opinion of the
committee, as per the requirement. The composition of
National Steering Committee is detailed in Annexure-C.
The NSC will have the following terms of reference:

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(i) Ensuring effective roll-out of PM Vishwakarma
across India.
(ii) Apex decision making body related to any aspect
concerning the Scheme.
(iii) Undertaking measures, as deemed appropriate,
and ensure delivery of Scheme benefits to the
eligible beneficiaries.
(iv) Approving any modifications required in the
Scheme including addition or deletion of trades.
(v) Engaging with stakeholders including civil
organisations, associations, forums etc. for
getting feedback about the Scheme.
(vi) Modifying the Scheme design, coverage, delivery
mechanism etc. within the overall mandate of the
Scheme.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
8.2 State Monitoring Committee (SMC)

The State Monitoring Committee (SMC) shall be
responsible for the operational implementation and
monitoring of the Scheme at the state level, it will also act as
a bridge between the NSC and the field level setup. The
SMC shall ensure the following:

(i) Co-ordination in roll out of the PM
Vishwakarma.
(ii) Active participation of stakeholder departments
and agencies of the State Governments
facilitating implementation of the Scheme.

(iii) To facilitate agencies of MSDE in providing Skill
Training to the beneficiaries.

(iv) To ensure coordination among banks and
financial institutions for smooth provisioning of
credit support to the beneficiaries.

(v) To facilitate IT-ITeS related support in
implementing the Scheme.

(vi) To create awareness about the Scheme at the
Gram Panchayat and Urban Local Body level in
the state.
(vii) To monitor the Scheme implementation and
share suggestions or feedback, if any, with the
National Steering Committee.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
The Committee shall be convened once in every quarter or
as per the requirement to discuss all the operational and
ground-level implementation matters under the Scheme.
The composition of the State Monitoring Committee is
detailed in Annexure-D.

8.3 District Implementation Committee

The District Implementation Committee shall be
responsible for the actual roll–out and implementation of
the Scheme at the field level and will coordinate with State
Government and other committees. The following are the
indicative terms of references of the District
Implementation Committee:

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(i) To ensure that enrolments of the beneficiaries
are seamlessly done by the CSCs in the Gram
Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies of the
district.
(ii) To ensure that verification of the enrolled
beneficiaries by Head of Gram Panchayats and
Executive Heads of Urban Local Bodies is done
in a smooth manner.
(iii) To ensure adequate awareness about the Scheme
in all Gram Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies.
It may put in place a suitable mechanism for the
purpose of ensuring that all eligible beneficiaries
are onboarded under the Scheme.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(iv) To conduct the Stage II verification of the
beneficiaries after Stage I verification from
Gram Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies.
(v) To ensure that all registered beneficiaries get
access to PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID
Cards.
(vi) To ensure that registered beneficiaries get
access to:
a. 5 days Basic Skill Training
b. Credit Support under the Scheme
c. Incentives for Digital Transaction
d. Marketing Support
(vi) The District Implementation Committee may
adopt suitable mechanism for ensuring that the
beneficiaries get seamless access to benefits
under the Scheme. The Committee may co-opt
two-three leading practitioners or domain
experts on honorary basis, with prior approval of
the National Steering Committee.
(vii) To ensure coordination with agencies of MSDE
for skill training and Tool kit distribution.
(viii) To ensure coordination with Banks and NBFCs,
etc. to facilitate credit support for the
beneficiaries.
(ix) To ensure that all suitable institutional
mechanism is put in place so that beneficiaries
can avail benefits that they are entitled to.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
(x) Take appropriate action on grievances of
beneficiaries related to the Scheme and share
feedback.

The Development and Facilitation Officers (DFOs) of
MoMSME shall work in close coordination with the
District Implementation Committee. The composition
of District Implementation Committee is detailed in
Annexure-E.

The Scheme will be implemented at the district level by
field level Implementing Agencies (IAs) through the
District Implementation Committee, under the
recommendation of the National Steering Committee
and the State Monitoring Committee. In view of the
number of beneficiaries to be covered under the PM
Vishwakarma Scheme, multiple IAs will be engaged for
the roll out. The details of IAs at the Central level and
State level are given at Annexure-F.

8.4 Credit Oversight Committee

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
The Credit Oversight Committee will be chaired by
Secretary (DFS) with Secretary (MoMSME) and
representative of Secretary (Expenditure), RBI, SIDBI and
CGTMSE as members. The Committee shall monitor
assured credit flow to the beneficiaries and ensure that the
credit is disbursed properly. The Credit Oversight
Committee shall be empowered to review and revise the
interest subvention cap under this Scheme keeping in view
the prevailing interest rates.

8.5 Roles and Responsibilities

Given the unique features of this Scheme, MSDE and DFS
shall be the co-executors of the Scheme along with
MoMSME. MSDE, DFS and MoMSME shall work in close
coordination for the successful implementation of the
Scheme, from identification of the beneficiaries to the
disbursal of funds, loans and marketing support. The roles
and responsibilities of various stakeholders are given
below:

9. Coordination with Ministries

The implementation of the Scheme will be done in
coordination with Ministry of Electronics and Information

Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Department for
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Department of

The support will be provided for the following:

(i) Identification of the beneficiaries.
(ii) Handholding and Registration of the
beneficiaries.
(iii) Awareness about the Scheme.

9.2 Coordination with Ministry of Labour &
Employment

Scheme has been given by the Ministry of Labour &

text:
10. Review and Monitoring

Monitoring of the implementation of the Scheme shall be
conducted on a regular basis through the National Steering
Committee and the State Monitoring Committee to
determine the progress under various components of the
Scheme. This shall be supported by a dedicated Programme
Management Unit (PMU) which shall be responsible for
monitoring the performance of IAs and the overall Scheme
implementation. An Online Monitoring System (OMS) shall
also be developed for approvals and monitoring of the
physical and financial progress of the Scheme. Some of the
key areas of monitoring shall be as follows:

(i) Achievement of milestones against timelines,
(ii) Utilization of funds as per the activities or amount as
indicated against the components,

(iii) Expenditure pattern as per the sequence of activities,

(iv) Output and outcome as per the defined indicators,

(v) Performance appraisal of IAs, and

(vi) Any other activity incidental to the above.

ministry_department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text:
The PM Vishwakarma portal shall also have the facility to
gather the beneficiary feedback and query resolution
mechanism to monitor the performance of the Scheme. A
helpline number shall also be setup at the central level to
support the beneficiaries in availing various incentives under
the Scheme.

Evaluation of the Scheme: It is envisaged to take-up third
party mid-term evaluation of the Scheme to determine the
gaps and take mid-course corrective measures. Impact
assessment studies shall also be undertaken at end of the
Scheme both at the IA-level and the Scheme level to validate
the outcomes achieved.

These Guidelines will be reviewed, revised and updated from
time to time by the National Steering Committee with the
approval of the Union Minister of MSME.

# Aadabidda Nidhi

## 1. Scheme Name

**Aadabidda Nidhi**

Also referred to as:

* **Aadabidda Nidhi Scheme**
* **Aadabidda Nidhi – Women’s Welfare Fund**

---

## 2. Scheme Status

**CURRENT_STATUS:** PROPOSED / UNDER REVIEW
**SOURCE_VERIFICATION_STATUS:** VERIFIED_PROPOSED_SCHEME — IMPLEMENTATION NOT CONFIRMED

Aadabidda Nidhi was announced as a proposed Andhra Pradesh women-welfare scheme with a promised benefit of **₹1,500 per month** for eligible women. However, the available 2026 reporting indicates that the scheme was still **under review and its implementation guidelines had not been finalized**. ([dailypioneer.com](https://www.dailypioneer.com/uploads/2025/epaper/september/vijayawada-english-edition-2025-09-27.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

The Government has therefore **not provided sufficient official evidence to classify it as an active 2026 beneficiary scheme**.

---

## 3. Objective

The proposed objective of Aadabidda Nidhi is to provide **regular financial assistance to eligible women in Andhra Pradesh** and support women's economic security and financial independence.

The scheme was included among the welfare commitments announced for women during the 2024 Andhra Pradesh election period. The documented proposed benefit was **₹1,500 per month**. ([dailypioneer.com](https://www.dailypioneer.com/uploads/2025/epaper/september/vijayawada-english-edition-2025-09-27.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 4. Target Beneficiaries

The publicly documented proposal identifies:

* **Women residing in Andhra Pradesh**
* Proposed age range: **18–59 years**

The ₹1,500/month benefit and 18–59 age range are repeatedly reported in available sources describing the proposal. ([orfonline.org](https://www.orfonline.org/research/cash-transfers-as-an-instrument-for-poverty-alleviation-and-womens-empowerment-in-india?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

However:

> **A final Government of Andhra Pradesh eligibility notification was not located confirming the complete beneficiary definition.**

Therefore, the RAG system must treat the age/category information as **proposed**, not as a deterministic current eligibility rule.

The most important finding for the RAG database is that **Aadabidda Nidhi should not currently be treated like Thalliki Vandanam, Deepam 2.0 or NTR Bharosa**.

In September 2025, the reported Legislative Council discussion stated that:

* The scheme was **under review**
* Estimates were being prepared
* **Procedural guidelines had not yet been finalized**. ([dailypioneer.com](https://www.dailypioneer.com/uploads/2025/epaper/september/vijayawada-english-edition-2025-09-27.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

February 2026 reporting likewise described the scheme as still being examined, with no confirmed launch date. ([aimindia.in](https://aimindia.in/aadabidda-nidhi-scheme-ap-women/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Therefore, the RAG record must preserve the distinction between:

**announced/proposed scheme**

and

**implemented welfare scheme**.

---

The following elements are documented as the proposed scheme:

* Name: Aadabidda Nidhi

([orfonline.org](https://www.orfonline.org/research/cash-transfers-as-an-instrument-for-poverty-alleviation-and-womens-empowerment-in-india?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 2. Scheme Overview

Annadata Sukhibhava is an Andhra Pradesh Government farmer welfare programme intended to provide financial support for agricultural investment and farmer-family needs.

The Andhra Pradesh Government's budget documents state that the scheme provides financial assistance of ₹20,000 per annum to farmers.

The Andhra Pradesh Government has also explicitly described the scheme as covering farmer families including tenant farmers and Recognition of Forest Rights (ROFR) farmers.

The central PM-KISAN component provides ₹6,000 per year to eligible landholding farmer families under the separate PM-KISAN eligibility rules.

### PM-KISAN Component

The Government of India identifies the following major exclusion categories:

- Institutional landholders
- Former and present holders of constitutional posts
- Former and present Ministers / State Ministers
- Former and present Members of Parliament
- Former and present Members of State Legislative Assemblies / Councils
- Former and present Mayors of Municipal Corporations
- Former and present Chairpersons of District Panchayats
- Serving or retired Central/State Government officers and employees
- Employees of Central/State Public Sector Enterprises
- Employees of autonomous institutions under government
- Regular employees of local bodies
- Retired pensioners receiving ₹10,000 or more per month, subject to the stated exceptions
- Persons who paid income tax in the previous assessment year
- Practising registered professionals including doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects

PM-KISAN also has specific land-record and family-level requirements.

These exclusions apply to the PM-KISAN component and must not automatically be represented as the complete exclusion list for the Andhra Pradesh state component.

# Deepam 2.0 Scheme

## 1. Basic Information

Scheme ID: AP_DEEPAM_2

Official Scheme Name: Deepam 2.0

State: Andhra Pradesh

Government: Government of Andhra Pradesh

Department:
Civil Supplies Department

Implementing Authority:
Civil Supplies Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh

Implementing Network:
LPG distributors / Oil Marketing Companies in coordination with
the Civil Supplies Department

Category:
Women / Household Welfare / LPG Subsidy

Subcategory:
Free LPG Refills

Scheme Status:
ACTIVE_CURRENT

Launch Date:
31 October 2024

Implementation Start:
01 November 2024

Current As Of:
September 2026

Scheme Type:
In-kind household benefit through LPG-cylinder subsidy/reimbursement

Important:
Deepam 2.0 should not be confused with the earlier Deepam LPG
connection scheme.

## 2. Scheme Overview

Deepam 2.0 is an Andhra Pradesh Government scheme under which
eligible households receive three LPG cylinder refills free of cost
per year.

The scheme was launched in October 2024 and implementation began
from 01 November 2024.

The Civil Supplies Department implements the scheme through the
existing LPG distribution network.

Current Andhra Pradesh government district information states that
three LPG refills are provided free of cost to LPG consumers who
have Rice Cards.

The scheme is therefore linked to:

- An active LPG connection
- A valid Rice Card
- Aadhaar-linked/validated beneficiary information
- LPG, Rice Card and Aadhaar data validation

The benefit is delivered through the LPG booking and reimbursement/
subsidy mechanism rather than as an unrestricted cash transfer.

## 3. Target Beneficiaries

Primary beneficiary:

Eligible households/consumers in Andhra Pradesh who:

- Have a valid Rice Card
- Have an active LPG connection
- Satisfy the required Aadhaar/data-validation conditions
- Have their LPG connection and household information successfully
 validated in the government system

The scheme is household/consumer based.

The currently verified government material does not establish a
separate universal age requirement for the beneficiary.

The scheme should therefore not be encoded as an age-based welfare
scheme.

## 4. Eligibility Criteria

### Rice Card

The beneficiary must have a valid Rice Card.

Current Andhra Pradesh district Civil Supplies information explicitly
states that Deepam-2 is implemented for LPG consumers who have Rice
Cards.

### LPG Connection

The beneficiary must have an active LPG connection in Andhra Pradesh.

The LPG connection must be successfully validated against the
government beneficiary database.

### Aadhaar

Aadhaar information is part of the beneficiary validation process.

The LPG connection, Rice Card and Aadhaar information are matched/
validated with relevant government databases.

Do not represent Aadhaar merely as an optional supporting document
when describing the beneficiary-validation mechanism.

### Residence

The verified implementation material establishes the beneficiary
through Andhra Pradesh's Rice Card and LPG databases.

A separate standalone domicile-age-income test was not identified
in the verified current scheme material.

Therefore:

Residence:
Andhra Pradesh beneficiary/database eligibility is required;
no separate numerical domicile criterion identified.

### Income

No separate numerical household-income threshold was identified in
the verified current Deepam-2 implementation material.

Therefore:

Income limit:
NOT SPECIFIED.

### Occupation

No occupation requirement was identified.

### Education

No education requirement was identified.

### Land

No landholding requirement was identified.

### Social Category

No caste-specific eligibility condition was identified.

Eligibility is primarily linked to Rice Card, LPG connection and
database validation.

### Family Requirement

The benefit is administered at the household/eligible LPG-consumer
level.

The current state survey and government implementation material
describe the benefit as three LPG cylinders per beneficiary family
per year.

## 5. Exclusions / Non-Eligibility

The following conditions can prevent a beneficiary from receiving the
Deepam-2 benefit:

- No valid Rice Card
- No active/eligible LPG connection
- LPG connection not successfully validated
- Rice Card information not successfully validated

### Important

Do not add the following as Deepam-2 exclusions unless supported by
a specific current Government Order or implementation guideline:

- Specific annual household income ceiling
- Land ceiling
- Vehicle ownership ceiling
- Electricity consumption ceiling
- Property-size ceiling
- Employment in government service
- Caste exclusion

These conditions are used in some other Andhra Pradesh welfare
schemes but were not established as universal Deepam-2 eligibility
rules in the verified material.

## 6. Benefits

### Primary Benefit

Three free LPG cylinder refills per eligible beneficiary family
per year.

### Annual Frequency

Maximum benefit:

3 LPG refills per year.

### Refill Schedule

From FY 2025-26 onward, the scheme operates on three four-month
blocks:

Block I:
April – July

Block II:
August – November

Block III:
December – March

One eligible cylinder is allocated per block.

This means the normal annual structure is:

- 1 cylinder during April–July
- 1 cylinder during August–November
- 1 cylinder during December–March

### Initial 2024-25 Provision

For the initial implementation year, the first cylinder could be
booked during the extended period from 29 October 2024 through
31 March 2025.

This initial booking window should not be confused with the normal
four-month block schedule used from FY 2025-26 onward.

### Benefit Delivery

The beneficiary books the LPG cylinder through the normal LPG
distribution system.

After delivery, the eligible subsidy/reimbursement is processed
through the government mechanism.

## 8. Application / Benefit Claim Process

Deepam 2.0 is primarily an entitlement/benefit-delivery scheme
rather than a conventional online welfare application.

### Normal Process

1. Beneficiary has a valid Rice Card.
2. Beneficiary has an active LPG connection.
3. LPG, Rice Card and Aadhaar information are validated.
4. Beneficiary books the eligible LPG cylinder.
5. LPG cylinder is delivered.
6. Eligible subsidy/reimbursement is processed.
7. Subsidy is credited to the beneficiary's bank account.

### KYC

KYC/data validation is important for beneficiaries whose LPG,
Aadhaar and Rice Card records are not already successfully matched.

Gas delivery personnel and local administration may facilitate
KYC/data correction activities.

### Grievance / Support

Government implementation material has identified the Civil Supplies
grievance mechanism and toll-free number 1967 for beneficiary
queries/complaints.

Beneficiaries may also approach the relevant local Secretariat /
Civil Supplies office where applicable.

Andhra Pradesh eligibility/validation rules.

Deepam-2 eligibility.

# Andhra Pradesh Housing / PMAY

## 1. Basic Information

Scheme ID:
AP_HOUSING_PMAY

Current Scheme Family:
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)

State:
Andhra Pradesh

Housing Coverage:
Rural + Urban

Current Components:

1. PMAY-G — Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin
2. PMAY-U 2.0 — Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban 2.0

Historical AP Programme:
Navaratnalu – Pedalandariki Illu /
Jagananna Housing Colonies

Category:

Important:
This record is an umbrella RAG record only.

Eligibility must be evaluated separately for:
- PMAY-G
- PMAY-U 2.0

Historical Pedalandariki Illu rules must not be used as current
PMAY-G or PMAY-U 2.0 eligibility rules.

## 2. Scheme Overview

The Andhra Pradesh housing programme is implemented through the
A.P. State Housing Corporation Limited (APSHCL) in coordination with
Government of India and Government of Andhra Pradesh housing
programmes.

APSHCL states that its objective is to assist BPL families in
constructing permanent/pucca houses.

The current housing framework includes:

### Rural

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G)

PMAY-G is the Government of India's rural housing programme for
eligible houseless households and households living in kutcha or
dilapidated houses.

### Urban

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0)

PMAY-U 2.0 provides housing assistance to eligible EWS/LIG/MIG
families living in urban areas.

PMAY-U 2.0 covers multiple implementation verticals including:

- Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC)
- Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP)
- Affordable Rental Housing
- Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS)

### Andhra Pradesh State Housing Programme

Navaratnalu–Pedalandariki Illu was an Andhra Pradesh flagship
housing/house-site programme launched under the previous state
government.

It included house-site distribution and housing construction in
layouts and own-site locations.

### Andhra Pradesh State Housing Programme

Navaratnalu–Pedalandariki Illu was an Andhra Pradesh flagship
housing/house-site programme launched under the previous state
government.

It included house-site distribution and housing construction in
layouts and own-site locations.

That historical programme must be retained separately from the
current PMAY-U 2.0/PMAY-G eligibility engines.

## 3. Target Beneficiaries

### PMAY-G

Primary target:

Rural households that are:

- Houseless, or
- Living in kutcha/dilapidated housing,

and satisfy the PMAY-G eligibility/selection criteria.

Beneficiary selection is based on the prescribed deprivation/
housing-status criteria and government verification.

### PMAY-U 2.0

Primary target:

Urban families belonging to:

- EWS
- LIG
- MIG

who satisfy the scheme's housing-ownership and other eligibility
conditions.

Current PMAY-U 2.0 income categories:

EWS:
Annual household income up to ₹3 lakh.

LIG:
Annual household income above ₹3 lakh and up to ₹6 lakh.

MIG:
Annual household income above ₹6 lakh and up to ₹9 lakh.

### Historical Pedalandariki Illu

Historical target beneficiaries included eligible weaker-section
families/households receiving:

- House-site pattas
- Houses in government-developed layouts
- Houses on own sites
- PMAY-linked housing assistance

## 4. Eligibility Criteria

# A. PMAY-G — Rural

### Rural Residence

The household must reside in a rural area.

### Housing Condition

PMAY-G is intended for households that:

- Do not have a shelter, or
- Live in a kutcha house, or
- Live in a dilapidated house,

subject to the complete PMAY-G eligibility/selection process.

### Pucca House

A household owning a pucca house is generally excluded.

### Number of Rooms

The official PMAY-G eligibility questionnaire asks whether the
house has more than two rooms.

A household with more than two rooms is excluded under the
PMAY-G eligibility filter.

### Motorised Vehicle

Households owning a motorised three-wheeler or four-wheeler are
excluded under the PMAY-G eligibility filter.

### Agricultural Machinery

Households owning mechanised three/four-wheeler agricultural
equipment are excluded.

All eligible beneficiaries/family members must have Aadhaar or

### Priority Groups

PMAY-U 2.0 gives preference to:

- Widows
- Single women
- Persons with Disabilities
- Senior citizens
- Transgender persons
- Scheduled Castes
- Scheduled Tribes
- Minorities
- Other weaker/vulnerable sections

Special focus includes:

- Safai Karmis
- Street vendors identified under PMSVANidhi
- Artisans under PM Vishwakarma
- Anganwadi workers
- Building and construction workers
- Residents of slums/chawls
- Other identified vulnerable groups

## 5. Exclusions / Non-Eligibility

# PMAY-G

The PMAY-G eligibility filter excludes households satisfying
specified exclusion conditions, including:

- Owning a pucca house
- House with more than two rooms
- Owning a motorised three/four-wheeler
- Owning mechanised agricultural equipment of the specified type
- Kisan Credit Card limit ₹50,000 or above
- Government employee in household
- Registered non-agricultural enterprise
- Household member earning more than ₹15,000/month
- Income-tax payer
- Professional-tax payer
- Irrigated land of 2.5 acres or more
- Unirrigated land of 5 acres or more

Other PMAY-G selection/deprivation criteria also apply.

# PMAY-U 2.0

A family is not eligible where:

- It already owns a pucca house anywhere in India.
- It received a house under a government/local-self-government
 housing scheme during the previous 20 years.
- It otherwise fails the applicable EWS/LIG/MIG and scheme-vertical
 conditions.
- It is seeking a benefit outside the applicable PMAY-U 2.0 vertical.

## 6. Benefits

# PMAY-G

PMAY-G provides assistance for construction of a pucca house.

The standard central assistance framework provides:

- ₹1.20 lakh in plain areas
- ₹1.30 lakh in specified hilly/difficult/IAP areas

The beneficiary may also receive convergence benefits such as:

- MGNREGS wage support
- Toilet assistance through the applicable sanitation programme
- Other convergence facilities

The exact AP implementation package may contain additional
State/GoAP support and material assistance.

# PMAY-U 2.0

PMAY-U 2.0 provides assistance according to the selected vertical.

### BLC

Beneficiary Led Construction supports eligible EWS families for
construction/enhancement of houses on eligible land.

### AHP

Affordable Housing in Partnership supports EWS housing in
public/private partnership projects.

### ARH

Affordable Rental Housing addresses rental housing needs of
eligible urban beneficiaries.

### ISS

Interest Subsidy Scheme provides interest subsidy on eligible
housing loans subject to PMAY-U 2.0 rules.

### Current AP PMAY-U 2.0 Evidence

Government of India sanction records show PMAY-U 2.0 central
assistance approved for Andhra Pradesh BLC projects during FY
2026-27.

Therefore PMAY-U 2.0 is currently operational in Andhra Pradesh.

## 8. Application / Selection Process

# PMAY-G

PMAY-G is not simply a first-come-first-served online housing
application.

The process involves:

1. Identification through prescribed rural housing/deprivation
 databases.
2. Verification of household conditions.
3. Gram Panchayat / local-level verification.
4. Preparation of eligible beneficiary list.
5. Approval under the prescribed administrative process.
6. Sanction of house.
7. Construction-stage monitoring.
8. Instalment payments linked to construction progress.
9. Geo-tagging/photographic monitoring.
10. Completion and convergence of basic amenities.

### AwaasPlus

AwaasPlus is used for identification/survey of additional eligible
rural households under the applicable PMAY-G process.

AwaasPlus 2024 provides survey and e-KYC functionality.

# PMAY-U 2.0

Urban beneficiaries are identified through:

- Urban Local Bodies
- State/UT housing authorities
- PMAY-U 2.0 MIS
- Demand surveys
- Beneficiary verification
- CSMC/project sanction process

For BLC, beneficiary and project details are submitted through the
State/ULB system and sanctioned through the prescribed PMAY-U 2.0
process.

government verification.

16. Verification Summary

### VERIFIED_CURRENT

PMAY-G:

- Current rural housing programme.
- Targets eligible rural houseless/kutcha/dilapidated-house
 households.
- Uses prescribed deprivation/eligibility filters.
- Includes government verification and construction-stage monitoring.

PMAY-U 2.0:

- Current urban housing programme.
- Covers EWS/LIG/MIG households.
- No pucca house anywhere in India.
- Previous government housing benefit within 20 years can exclude.
- Aadhaar/Aadhaar Virtual ID integration is required.
- PMAY-G/PMAY-U duplication is checked.
- Preference is given to specified vulnerable groups.
- Andhra Pradesh has current PMAY-U 2.0 BLC sanctions in FY 2026-27.

### HISTORICAL

- Navaratnalu–Pedalandariki Illu
- Jagananna Housing Colonies
- PMAY-YSR branding
- Historical state-specific housing benefit structures

### DO NOT HARD-CODE

- Historical Pedalandariki Illu income rules as PMAY-U 2.0 rules.
- Historical PMAY-YSR assistance amounts as current PMAY-U 2.0
 assistance.
- One eligibility test for both rural and urban beneficiaries.
- One benefit amount for all PMAY verticals.

## 17. Notes and Limitations

1. "Andhra Pradesh Housing / PMAY" is an umbrella category, not one
 single beneficiary rule.

2. PMAY-G and PMAY-U 2.0 must be separate eligibility engines.

3. Rural/urban jurisdiction is the first major branching condition.

4. PMAY-U 2.0 has multiple verticals with different benefit
 mechanisms.

5. PMAY-G selection is based on prescribed rural housing/deprivation
 criteria and government verification.

6. PMAY-U 2.0 uses income categories EWS/LIG/MIG.

7. PMAY-U 2.0's no-pucca-house condition applies anywhere in India.

8. Previous government housing benefit within 20 years is an
 important PMAY-U 2.0 exclusion.

9. Current central assistance does not necessarily equal the total
 value of the house received by an Andhra Pradesh beneficiary.

10. State/GoAP contributions and convergence benefits must be stored
 separately from Central assistance.

11. Historical Navaratnalu–Pedalandariki Illu should not be merged
 with PMAY-U 2.0.

## 2. Scheme Overview

Jagananna Chedodu was introduced by the Government of Andhra Pradesh
to provide financial assistance to traditional service-occupation
workers.

The scheme covers:

- Rajakas / washermen
- Nayee Brahmins / barbers
- Tailors

The original Government Order sanctioned financial assistance of
₹10,000 per year to eligible persons having shops and engaged in
their respective traditional occupations.

The objective was to provide economic assistance and support the
livelihood/self-employment activities of these workers.

The scheme was implemented through the Backward Classes Welfare
administration and district-level BC Welfare machinery.

Persons engaged in washing/laundry work.

### Nayee Brahmins

Persons engaged in barber/hair-cutting services.

### Tailors

Persons engaged in tailoring work.

The official district BC Corporation description states that
Rajakas, Nayee Brahmins and Tailors belonging to all communities
were covered, subject to the applicable scheme conditions.

Therefore the occupation is a core eligibility condition.

The scheme is NOT a general-purpose financial assistance programme
for all BC households.

## 4. Eligibility Criteria

### Occupation

The applicant must belong to one of the covered traditional
occupations:

- Rajaka / washerman
- Nayee Brahmin / barber
- Tailor

The applicant should be actively engaged in the relevant occupation.

### Shop / Establishment

The original Government Order description specifies eligible
beneficiaries as persons having shops and living on the relevant
profession.

Therefore the applicant's livelihood activity/business establishment
is an important eligibility factor.

Do not assume that merely possessing the relevant caste/community
certificate automatically qualifies a person.

### Community / Caste

The official district BC Corporation description states that
Rajakas, Nayee Brahmins and Tailors belonging to all communities
are covered.

scheme description for the three occupations.

However, occupation must be established.

### Residence

The scheme is an Andhra Pradesh Government scheme.

The beneficiary must be identified through the applicable Andhra
Pradesh government/local beneficiary system.

### EBC Nestham

EBC Nestham is a separate livelihood-support programme.

Jagananna Thodu is a separate working-capital support programme
for street vendors, small traders and traditional-artisan
businesses.

BC Corporation loan/subsidy programmes are separate from Chedodu's

# Jnanabhumi Post-Matric Scholarships (RTF/MTF)

## 1. Basic Information

Post Matric Scholarships (RTF/MTF)

Jnanabhumi

Andhra Pradesh

Government of Andhra Pradesh

Social Welfare Department

- Social Welfare
- Tribal Welfare

- Minority Welfare

- Differently Abled Welfare
- Other designated welfare authorities

Important Naming Note:
The current Jnanabhumi portal presents the programme as
"Post Matric Scholarships (RTF/MTF)".

The terms Jagananna Vidya Deevena and Jagananna Vasathi Deevena
refer to the RTF and MTF components respectively under the
post-matric scholarship framework.

Do not create three independent schemes from these names.

## 2. Scheme Overview

The Andhra Pradesh Post Matric Scholarship programme provides
financial assistance to eligible students pursuing post-matric
education.

The current Jnanabhumi portal states that the scheme is implemented
on a saturation basis for eligible students belonging to:

- SC
- ST
- BC
- EBC (other than Kapu)
- Kapu
- Minority
- Differently Abled

The programme has two major components:

### RTF — Reimbursement of Tuition Fee

RTF provides reimbursement of eligible tuition and other approved
fees according to the applicable fee structure and Government Orders.

The current Jnanabhumi portal describes RTF as full fee reimbursement
for eligible students.

### MTF — Maintenance / Food and Hostel Assistance

MTF provides annual maintenance assistance:

- ITI: ₹10,000 per student
- Polytechnic: ₹15,000 per student
- Degree and above: ₹20,000 per student

The current Jnanabhumi portal states that MTF is intended for food
and hostel expenses.

## 3. Target Beneficiaries

Eligible students pursuing post-matric courses.

The current Jnanabhumi portal identifies the following beneficiary

1. Scheduled Caste (SC)
2. Scheduled Tribe (ST)
3. Backward Classes (BC)
4. Economically Backward Classes (EBC), other than Kapu
5. Kapu
6. Minority
7. Differently Abled

The programme is intended for students pursuing eligible
post-matric education in recognised institutions.

## 4. Eligibility Criteria

### Course Level

Eligible courses include:

- ITI
- Polytechnic
- Degree
- Degree and above-level courses

The current Jnanabhumi portal specifically describes Polytechnic,
ITI and Degree & above courses.

Intermediate is not treated as a post-matric scholarship course
under this current scheme record.

### Institution

Eligible students may study in:

- Government colleges/institutions
- Aided colleges/institutions
- Eligible private colleges
- Institutions affiliated to State Universities / Boards

The institution must satisfy the applicable recognition,
affiliation and Jnanabhumi requirements.

### Attendance

The current Jnanabhumi portal states:

75% aggregate attendance is mandatory for release of scholarships.

In addition, G.O.Ms.No.87 dated 20-11-2024 states that:

- From AY 2024-25, RTF for students other than SC students is
 released to college accounts according to the revised guidelines.
- From AY 2025-26, RTF for students other than SC students is
 subject to FRS attendance in colleges.
- SC RTF continues to be released to student accounts according to
 the applicable Government of India guidelines.

### Family Income

The current Jnanabhumi scheme page specifies:

Total family annual income:
Less than or equal to ₹2.50 lakh.

This is the principal income threshold currently displayed by the

### Landholding

The current Jnanabhumi portal specifies that family landholding
must be within the prescribed limits:

- Less than 10 acres wet land, OR
- Less than 25 acres dry land, OR
- Less than 25 acres combined wet and dry land.

Important:
The portal's wording should be preserved exactly in the eligibility
engine because older application forms contain a different
presentation of the land condition.

### Government Employment / Pension

No family member should be a government employee or pensioner.

Exception:
Sanitary workers are exempt from this exclusion irrespective of
salary/recruitment, subject to the applicable certification process.

### Four-Wheeler

No family member should own a four-wheeler.

Exemptions include:

- Taxi
- Tractor
- Auto

as specified by the Jnanabhumi eligibility rules.

### Urban Property

The current Jnanabhumi portal states that the family is eligible
where it owns no property or less than 1500 square feet of built-up
area in urban areas.

Therefore:

Urban property threshold:
Less than 1500 sq ft.

### Income Tax

No family member should be an income-tax payer.

information.

The application form records AP local nativity under Article 371-D.

to the qualifying course for the indicated local-nativity test.

7. Welfare department verifies eligibility.
8. Scholarship is sanctioned according to the applicable rules.
9. RTF/MTF is released through the applicable payment mechanism.

## 2. Scheme Overview

NTR Bharosa Pension Scheme is the Government of Andhra Pradesh's social security pension programme for eligible vulnerable and economically disadvantaged beneficiaries.

The scheme provides monthly financial assistance to specified beneficiary categories including old-age persons, widows, persons with disabilities, weavers, toddy tappers, fishermen, single women, transgender persons, traditional cobblers, Dappu artists, ARTPLHIV beneficiaries and specified medical-condition categories.

The scheme name was restored to NTR Bharosa Pension Scheme through G.O.Ms.No.43 dated 13.06.2024.

The enhanced pension rates ordered through the 2024 Government Order became applicable from July 2024, with the ₹4,000 category receiving arrears as specified in the Government Order.

Current operational status is supported by the official NTR Bharosa dashboard, which records pension disbursements for September 2026.

## 4. Eligibility Criteria

### Common Eligibility Conditions

The official NTR Bharosa portal specifies the following common conditions

- The proposed beneficiary shall be from a BPL family holding a white ration card.
- The beneficiary shall be a local resident of the district.
- The beneficiary shall not be covered under another pension scheme.

These common conditions should be interpreted together with the category-specific eligibility conditions and applicable exclusion factors.

### Age

#### Old Age Pension

- Male or female.
- 60 years of age or above.
- The official portal also describes the beneficiary as destitute, meaning having little or no means of subsistence and no family or relative to depend upon.

#### Weavers Pension

- 50 years of age or above.
- The official portal describes the beneficiary as destitute.

#### Widow Pension

- 18 years and above, according to the current official NTR Bharosa eligibility page.

#### Disabled Pension

# Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Scheme

## 1. Basic Information

Scheme ID: AP_NTR_VAIDYA_SEVA

Official Scheme Name:
Dr. Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao Vaidya Seva Scheme
(Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva)

Common Reference:
NTR Vaidya Seva

State:
Andhra Pradesh

Government:
Government of Andhra Pradesh

Department:
Health, Medical & Family Welfare Department

Implementing Authority:
Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust

Category:
Health / Medical Assistance / Health Protection

Subcategory:
Cashless Secondary and Tertiary Healthcare

Scheme Type:
State-sponsored healthcare assurance / cashless treatment

Current Status:
ACTIVE_CURRENT

Current As Of:
September 2026

Original Scheme Launch:
01 April 2007

Important Historical Note:
The Government of Andhra Pradesh renamed the former Rajiv Aarogyasri
Scheme as Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva after the reorganisation of Andhra
Pradesh.

Important Verification Note:
Current Andhra Pradesh government sources do not expose identical
scheme statistics. The H&MFW state page contains older coverage
figures, while a current district government page describes a
₹5 lakh family-floater and 3,257 listed therapies.

Therefore, the RAG must not treat the older figures as current.

## 2. Scheme Overview

Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is a state-sponsored healthcare scheme of the
Government of Andhra Pradesh intended to provide financial protection
and cashless healthcare to eligible poor/BPL families.

The scheme provides:

- Cashless medical treatment
- Secondary and tertiary healthcare
- Treatment for specified diseases/procedures
- Services through empanelled network hospitals
- Government hospitals and eligible private/corporate hospitals
- Pre-treatment evaluation where applicable
- Hospitalisation and treatment packages
- Post-discharge follow-up services where applicable

The scheme is administered through the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.

The scheme is designed to reduce catastrophic medical expenditure
for eligible poor families.

Eligible patients can receive treatment through empanelled network
hospitals.

Help desks staffed by Vaidya Mithras are provided at relevant
healthcare facilities to assist beneficiaries.

## 3. Target Beneficiaries

The scheme is intended to provide healthcare protection to poor

Do not interpret the scheme as automatically covering every resident
of Andhra Pradesh.

Eligibility depends on the beneficiary database and applicable
government rules.

beneficiaries linked with Aadhaar.

identification and authentication.

Do not represent Aadhaar as an independent income-eligibility test.

### Residence

The scheme is an Andhra Pradesh Government programme for eligible
beneficiaries in the Andhra Pradesh beneficiary database.

No separate numerical residence-duration requirement was identified
in the current verified material.

### Income

The scheme uses BPL/eligible beneficiary identification.

A current universal numerical household-income ceiling was not
established from the authoritative current sources reviewed.

Therefore:

At the hospital, the beneficiary's eligibility is authenticated

Emergency registration and treatment are supported under the scheme
for eligible listed therapies, with the hospital obtaining the
required authorisation according to scheme procedures.

## 8. Application / Treatment Process

Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is not primarily a conventional online welfare
application.

### Normal Process

1. Beneficiary approaches a government facility, health camp,
 network hospital or relevant healthcare point.
2. Beneficiary identity is verified.
3. Medical condition is assessed.
4. If the disease/treatment is covered, the patient is referred/
 registered for the appropriate package.
5. Network hospital obtains required authorisation.
6. Treatment is provided cashlessly.
7. Discharge and post-discharge services are provided according to
 the approved package.
8. Claims are processed through the Trust's online system.

### Vaidya Mithra

Vaidya Mithras/help desks assist beneficiaries at relevant
healthcare facilities.

They help patients with:

- Eligibility verification
- Registration
- Scheme information

# Stree Shakti Scheme

## 1. Basic Information

Scheme ID: AP_STREE_SHAKTI

Official Scheme Name: Stree Shakti Scheme

Official Description:
Free Bus Travel for Women Scheme – Stree Shakti Scheme

State: Andhra Pradesh

Government: Government of Andhra Pradesh

Department:
Transport, Roads & Buildings Department

Implementing Agency:
Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) /
Andhra Pradesh Public Transport Department (APPTD)

Category: Women Welfare / Public Transport

Subcategory: Free Public Transport

15 August 2025

G.O.Ms.No.27, Transport, Roads & Buildings (PTD.I) Department,

Current Operational Evidence:
The official APSRTC website continues to list Stree Shakti under its
current passenger schemes/coverage information.

Important 2026 Update:
G.O.Ms.No.21 dated 28.02.2026 separately extended free travel to
eligible persons with disabilities in Stree Shakti-covered bus services,
with a 50% concession for eligible escorts.

## 2. Scheme Overview

Stree Shakti is an Andhra Pradesh Government free public-transport
scheme launched on 15 August 2025.

The original scheme provides free travel to:

- Girls
- Women
- Transgender persons

who have Andhra Pradesh domicile status and produce valid identity proof.

The original scheme operates in specified APSRTC bus services.

The Government Order specifies that the scheme is implemented across
Andhra Pradesh.

The scheme is intended to improve mobility and access to:

- Education
- Employment
- Healthcare
- Other essential activities

The Government reimburses APSRTC for the eligible zero-fare travel
provided under the scheme.

The scheme should be represented as a transport-benefit programme,
not as a cash-transfer scheme.

## 3. Target Beneficiaries

### Original Stree Shakti Beneficiaries

The original Government Order identifies:

- Girls
- Women
- Transgender individuals

with Andhra Pradesh domicile status.

A valid identity document must be produced.

Eligible beneficiaries receive zero-fare tickets on covered APSRTC
services.

### Covered Services

The original Government Order identifies five service categories:

1. Pallevelugu
2. Ultra Pallevelugu
3. City Ordinary
4. Metro Express
5. Express

### Enclave Routes

Eligible beneficiaries are permitted to travel free on enclave route
services.

### Travel Area

The original scheme is a statewide Andhra Pradesh transport scheme.

The beneficiary can travel within Andhra Pradesh on eligible covered
services.

Interstate services are excluded.

### Number of Journeys

No numerical daily/monthly journey limit is specified in the verified
Government Order.

Therefore:

Journey limit:
Not specified.

### Cash Benefit

There is no direct cash payment to beneficiaries.

The benefit is free transportation.

### Government Reimbursement

The Government reimburses APSRTC based on eligible zero-fare tickets
issued under the scheme.

## 7. Required Documents

The original Government Order requires:

- Valid identity proof.

The current APSRTC scheme page also states that eligible beneficiaries
must produce valid ID proof.

The exact list of acceptable identity documents should be taken from
the current APSRTC implementation system.

Potential identity documents may include government-issued identity
documents where accepted by APSRTC.

Do not mark Aadhaar as the only universally mandatory document unless
the current APSRTC implementation guideline explicitly states this.

No income certificate is required under the verified original scheme.

No caste certificate is required under the verified original scheme.

No land document is required under the verified original scheme.

## 8. Application Process

Stree Shakti is primarily a travel entitlement rather than a
cash-benefit application scheme.

### Normal Travel Process

1. Beneficiary travels on an eligible Stree Shakti service.
2. Beneficiary produces valid identity proof when required.
3. Conductor verifies eligibility/identity.
4. A zero-fare ticket is issued.
5. Beneficiary travels without paying the normal fare.

# Thalliki Vandanam Scheme

## 1. Basic Information

Scheme ID: AP_THALLIKI_VANDANAM

Official Scheme Name: Thalliki Vandanam

State: Andhra Pradesh

Government: Government of Andhra Pradesh

Department: School Education Department

Category: Education / Student Welfare

Subcategory: Educational Financial Assistance

Implementing Departments / Agencies:
- School Education Department
- Director of School Education
- Director of Intermediate Education
- State Project Director, Samagra Shiksha
- School Infrastructure / Mid-Day Meal & related education authorities
- Society for Grama/Ward Secretariats (SGSW)
- Welfare Departments / Welfare Corporations
- District Collectors
- APCFSS / RTGS for payment-related functions

Scheme Status: ACTIVE_CURRENT

Current As Of: September 2026

Academic Year Covered:
2026-27

Original Implementation:
2025-26

Current Governing Order:
G.O.Ms.No.15, School Education (Ser.I) Department,
dated 16.07.2026.

Administrative Sanction:
G.O.Ms.No.16, School Education (Ser.I) Department,
dated 16.07.2026.

Historical Relationship:
The programme follows the earlier Andhra Pradesh school-education financial-assistance framework associated with Amma Vodi, but the current scheme should be represented independently as Thalliki Vandanam.

Important:
Do not merge historical Amma Vodi eligibility and current Thalliki Vandanam rules unless the applicable government order explicitly carries the rule forward.

## 2. Scheme Overview

Thalliki Vandanam is an Andhra Pradesh Government educational financial-assistance programme intended to support children continuing education from Class I through Class XII, including Intermediate Education.

The scheme provides financial assistance to an eligible mother or recognised guardian for each eligible child.

The scheme applies to eligible students studying in:

- Government schools
- Private aided schools
- Private unaided schools
- Recognised residential schools
- Recognised junior colleges / residential junior colleges

The scheme was implemented from academic year 2025-26 and was continued for academic year 2026-27 through G.O.Ms.No.15 dated 16.07.2026.

The scheme was implemented from academic year 2025-26 and was continued for academic year 2026-27 through G.O.Ms.No.15 dated 16.07.2026.

The benefit is ₹15,000 per eligible child per academic year.

An amount of ₹2,000 per student is deducted at source for the educational ecosystem, including school/junior-college maintenance, hygiene and sanitation and other purposes prescribed under the applicable SOP.

Therefore, the normal amount credited to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-seeded bank account is ₹13,000, subject to special payment arrangements such as RTE Section 12(1)(c) and scholarship convergence.

## 3. Target Beneficiaries

Primary beneficiary:

- Eligible mother of a child studying in Classes I-XII / Intermediate.

Recognised guardian:

- Where the mother is unavailable or where the applicable rules recognise another guardian, the benefit may be paid to the recognised guardian subject to the scheme's verification process.

Student coverage:

- Class I
- Classes II-XII
- Intermediate / Junior Intermediate
- Recognised residential school/junior-college students
- Eligible students in Government schools
- Eligible students in Private Aided schools
- Eligible students in Private Unaided schools

Special categories:

- Single-parent families
- Orphan children
- Street children enrolled through eligible voluntary organisations
- Children admitted under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act, 2009
- Students covered under certain Centrally Sponsored Scholarship Schemes, subject to the scheme's balance-payment rules

The benefit is calculated per eligible child rather than once per family.

## 4. Eligibility Criteria

### Age

No separate beneficiary age limit for the mother/guardian is specified in the verified scheme guidelines.

Eligibility is primarily linked to the student's class, enrolment and household eligibility.

- Intermediate / Junior Intermediate

### Gender

The ordinary beneficiary is the mother of the eligible child.

However, the scheme also recognises guardians and provides special provisions for:

- Single-parent families
- Cases where the mother is unavailable
- Orphan children

Therefore, the benefit is not implemented as a strict female-only payment rule in every circumstance.

Payment recipient is determined according to the applicable mother/guardian rules.

### Residence

The beneficiary should be included in the relevant Andhra Pradesh household database.

The 2026 guidelines provide for field verification where the beneficiary is not present in the household database but the child is present.

The student must be studying in a recognised institution covered by the Andhra Pradesh scheme.

State:
